claim: This paper examines the effectiveness of the time series momentum strategy in generating positive returns in the US stock market, with a focus on exploring its dynamics and performance using different moving average methods.
universe: The data set used in this study was from the S&P500 index, which includes daily closing prices of its constituent stocks.

horizon.reason: les passages fournis ne précisent pas le horizon de prévision du modèle

signal_construction: After fitting the regression model, a momentum trading strategy that generates portfolio weights based on the simple moving average (MA) or exponential moving average (EMA) of asset returns was developed.

what_is_missing: Les passages fournis ne précisent pas les tests de significativité statistique des performances, les coûts de transaction détaillés au niveau intraday, les paramètres exacts de décay pour les EMA, ni les poids de portefeuille spécifiques attribués à chaque actif.

source.title: Performance of Time-series Momentum Strategy: US

what_transfers: use of simple and exponential moving averages as momentum signals
linear regression framework for predicting next‑day returns
evaluation of strategies via Sharpe ratio
what_does_not_transfer: transaction‑cost rates calibrated for equity trading are not directly applicable to futures
the S&P500 constituent universe differs from futures contracts
the 24‑day look‑back period may be unsuitable for intraday futures horizons
what_aligns_well: relative ranking of EMA versus MA strategies persists across asset classes
sensitivity of performance to increasing transaction costs shows a similar degradation pattern
the benefit of EMA over MA in certain windows is observed in both equities and futures
